findings.issue: writeStockOrCompensate calls zeroStock on every RuntimeException. That includes failures where nothing reached inventory: the local quantity<0 ValidationException thrown inside writeStock after offerService.create in createOffer, and a definitive inventory 400. zeroStock overwrites the row and does not restore it. Under a PLATFORM ctx (an admin adding a platform offer to an existing product, createOffer:179-191), it writes 0 to the platform row (offer_id NULL) at that warehouse. Any pre-existing legacy platform stock there is wiped and shiftLegacyTotals publishes a quantity event, even though no stock write was intended. For sellers the impact is limited to their own rows, e.g. orphan rows left by an earlier discarded offer. There is no cross-tenant effect, because the sellerId comes from the server-side offer and inventory rows are keyed by seller.
findings.fix: Zero only when the outcome is unknown: catch UpstreamUnavailableException for zero+undo and run undo alone for ValidationException. Also validate quantity>=0 in createOffer before offerService.create so no offer and no stock call happen for bad input.

findings.issue: The sellerId now sent on each reserve Item defaults to Order.PLATFORM_SELLER when the chosen offer has offerId set but sellerId null in the product view (603-605). In slice 2, inventory keeps the platform fallback exactly when sellerId==PLATFORM, so this default fails open: a seller offer with a missing owner field would be served from platform stock. Today the value is server-derived from product-service, not client input, and inventory ignores it in this slice, so it cannot be exploited yet.
findings.fix: When offerId != null and offer.sellerId() == null, send sellerId null on the StockLine (keep PLATFORM on the order line if needed for display). Inventory's pre-transaction SellerDirectory lookup then resolves the owner and fails closed.

findings.issue: Pre-existing, not introduced by this diff. The internal setStock path used by product-service passes anyWarehouse=true, so resolveWarehouse (174) never raises 403. A seller can name another seller's or a platform warehouse code in create/bulk/zeroStock and get their own seller-keyed row placed there. Other tenants' quantities are not changed. The 'Forbidden -> warehouseCode' mapping in SellerCatalogService.writeStock is unreachable on this path, which contradicts the requirements' section 6 claim that the 403 check protects this flow.
findings.fix: Backlog item: have setStock enforce w.sellerId()==sellerId unless sellerId is PLATFORM, or pass an explicit admin flag from product-service.

findings.issue: Pre-existing: bulk row errors echo the raw RuntimeException message to the seller, which can include SQL or constraint text from compensation or repository failures. The new UpstreamUnavailableException wrapping makes Feign failures safe ('Upstream service unavailable: inventory-service'; the cause is not serialized). Other runtime errors still pass through unfiltered.
findings.fix: Map non-ApplicationException RuntimeExceptions to a generic 'row failed' message plus a correlation id, and log the details server-side.

summary: No blocker or major issues in slice 1. Cross-tenant stock: every stock write and the new zeroStock compensation use offer.getSellerId() and offer.getId() from the server-side offer created in the same call, and inventory rows are keyed by seller, so one seller cannot change or zero another seller's rows. Platform rows can be zeroed only under a PLATFORM (admin) ctx (minor 1). discard() and catalog.delete() have no ownership checks, but neither is reachable from a controller, and they are called only on ids created in the same request. The reserve sellerId comes from product-service's offer through chooseOffer, which rejects offerIds that are not on the product, so a buyer cannot forge it. The PLATFORM default for a null owner should become null before the slice-2 inventory fail-closed lands (minor 2). Forged or replayed events: product-service now skips any QUANTITY_CHANGED that carries an offerId, so a forged seller-scoped event changes nothing. Events without an offerId keep the pre-existing Kafka trust model, unchanged. The new 503 uses UpstreamUnavailableException, which exposes only the upstream name; ProblemPayloadFactory hides the cause, and the existing test checks this. Bulk CSV: the in-file de-dup key is trim+upper(Locale.ROOT). The seen-set is bounded by the unchanged 1000-row / 2 MB limits, and blank SKUs still fail at require(). No dependency additions, secrets or PII in the diff. Logs carry only offerId and productId. Note: slice 1 does not include the inventory fail-closed reservation, so the platform-stock oversell fallback stays open until slice 2.
